attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, not a quote of anyone else.

semantics.note: This is a firm, unhedged present-tense observation with two parts. It covers both Copilot and Gemini: the consumer push failed, and billions were spent. The drafter's wording keeps both parts and the scope of both companies.

contract.note: The relative reading of 'failed' is fair and ordinary. It is anchored in the speaker's own 'meaningful consumer penetration' setup. Reading 'burning billions' as AI capital spending since 2023 follows his own context. With no threshold for 'failed', the result still depends on interpretation.

evidence.note: October 2024 court exhibit: Gemini had about 90M monthly users. That is within the period. Under the contract's relative reading it is small next to Google's reach and rival chatbots. On an absolute reading it would cut against the claim.
Meta AI had about 500M monthly users and ChatGPT over 400M weekly users. This supports the view that Gemini lagged its rivals. The Meta figure is from September 2024, just before the window.
The March 2025 figure of 350M monthly users is after the target period, so it is context only. It shows fast growth just after the post.

reviews.rationale: The Gemini part has support under the contract's relative reading. The packet has no consumer Copilot usage data for the period and no evidence of spending on these consumer efforts. The speaker's own figures cannot prove themselves. Two of the claim's components (Copilot uptake and 'burning billions') are unchecked, so the claim as a whole is not settled by this evidence.
